I've run correspondent banking relationships in London for fifteen years, and every important partnership starts with a bilateral meeting. Here's how I run them. First, I send a short agenda a week before, with five points, never more. Second, in the room, I don't present for twenty minutes. I talk for three, and then I hand the floor over with a real question, something like, how does this look from your side? Third, I never try to close everything on the first day. We agree on the problem, we agree on a framework, and we leave the commercial details for a working group. And finally, before anyone leaves, I read the next steps out loud, with names and dates. If it isn't said in the room, it doesn't happen.

Hello Fabio, this is Marco Ferri, legal counsel at Main River Bank in Frankfurt. I'm calling about the draft memorandum of understanding. Good news first. Our side has reviewed the document, and we're happy with the structure. There are still two points we need to iron out: the governance of the working group, and who pays for the testing environment. Our plan is this. By the end of next week, we'll have sent you our comments in writing. And by the time we meet in Frankfurt, I hope both legal teams will have agreed on a final version. Please call me back when you have a moment. Thank you.
